anomalies.observed: On the POWER TRAIN sheet (page 1, row A) the high-side series element on the 24 V input path, annotated 'Reverse polarity protection', is T3 = AON6407, an N-channel MOSFET, with its gate pulled down to GND through R7 33k and its two terminals in series between the post-fuse node (+24V_FB) and the +24V bulk rail.
anomalies.expected: A high-side series reverse-polarity switch must be a P-channel MOSFET (gate referenced to the input negative rail), as was used in r1 (SI2301 P-MOSFET per spec §5). The specification's own component table also assigns AON6407 to a low-side role, not a high-side series element: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch'. An N-channel device cannot turn on when its gate is tied to GND while its source sits at +24 V.

evidence.quote: POWER TRAIN, page 1 row A: 'Reverse polarity protection' label over T3 'AON6407' placed in series on the +24V path, gate to GND via R7 33k
§2 Component Table: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch'
§5 r1→r2: 'r1's BOM lists ... T1 SI2301 P-MOSFET' (the P-channel part previously used for reverse-polarity protection)

anomalies.impact: With Vgs ≈ -24 V (gate at GND, source at +24 V) the N-channel T3 never enhances; the 24 V rail is fed only through the body diode (≈0.7 V drop and heating at load current) or not at all depending on orientation, and the gate sees a voltage beyond the ±20 V AON6407 rating. The intended reverse-polarity protection and clean 24 V pass-through do not behave as designed.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the documented architecture, but the high-side reverse-polarity protection element T3 is an N-channel AON6407 (which the spec reserves for a low-side switch), a part type that cannot function as a grounded-gate high-side series switch; this is the one deviation the drawing supports.
